english: Let $y=y(x)$, $x>-1$, be the solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{2x-2y-1}{2x-2y}$ with $y(0)=-1$. Then the value of $y\left(\dfrac{21}{4}\right)$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $y=y(x)$, $x>-1$, अवकल समीकरण $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{2x-2y-1}{2x-2y}$ का वह हल है जिसके लिए $y(0)=-1$ है। तब $y\left(\dfrac{21}{4}\right)$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Numerator and denominator lines are parallel; the right side is a function of $u=x-y$
solution_full: The lines $2x-2y-1=0$ and $2x-2y=0$ are parallel, so no shift of origin makes the equation homogeneous. Instead, the right side is a function of $x-y$ only: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{2u-1}{2u}$ with $u=x-y$.
At $x=0$: $u=0-(-1)=1$, so $c=1$ and $u^{2}=x+1$. Since $u(0)=1>0$ and $u$ cannot pass through $0$ (the equation is undefined there), $u=\sqrt{x+1}$ on $x>-1$.
originality_note: New: an equation that looks like the reducible-to-homogeneous type but has parallel lines, so the substitution u = x - y is forced and gives u^2 = x + 1. Closest known: dy/dx = (x - y + 1)/(x - y - 1) type exercises. Different because: the resulting equation is u u' = 1/2 with a square-root solution, read at a point where the root is rational.
blueprint_concepts: Equations reducible to variable separable: dy/dx = f(ax + by + c)

concept_use.Equations reducible to variable separabl: The right side depends only on x - y (the two lines are parallel), so u = x - y turns the equation into du/dx = 1/(2u), which is separable.

Changed: No change.
key_step: Notice parallel lines, set u = x - y, get u^2 = x + 1.
justification: A standard substitution and a one-line separable integration; routine but with the parallel-lines decision. Comparable to 2026-P2-Q3 (L2).
